analog: Spread of true vs false news on Twitter 2006-2017 (Vosoughi, Roy & Aral, Science 2018), with fact-check lag from Hoaxy (Shao et al., WWW 2016)

sources.title: Vosoughi S., Roy D., Aral S., The spread of true and false news online, Science 359:1146-1151 (2018)
VOA Learning English: Study: False News Spreads Faster and Farther than Truth (2018), reporting ~10 h vs ~60 h to reach 1,500 users
Shao C., Ciampaglia G.L., Flammini A., Menczer F., Hoaxy: A Platform for Tracking Online Misinformation, WWW '16 Companion (2016)
Science news: Fake news spreads faster than true news on Twitter, thanks to people, not bots (2018)

points.notes: average false story reaches 1,500 users in ~10 h

comparison_true_news.notes: average true story reaches 1,500 users in ~60 h (six times longer, s1)

threat.notes: extent = share of a 1,500-person audience reached (the paper's own benchmark). Only endpoints are sourced; no doubling time was found, so draw the path between with a stated monotone ease, or use the paper's figure. Other sourced ratios (s1): truth takes ~20x longer than falsehood to reach cascade depth 10; falsehoods are 70% more likely to be retweeted; top 1% of false cascades reached 1,000-100,000 people while true ones rarely exceeded 1,000. Dataset: ~126,000 cascades, ~3 million people, >4.5 million tweets.

fragments.who: independent fact-checking organizations (six used in the study)
fragments.notes: fact-check sharing lags misinformation by ~13 h in aggregate

fragments.who: people who already knew the true version
fragments.notes: true stories exist in the same network; they just travel slower

fragments.had: the choice to share or not
fragments.notes: study found humans, not bots, drove the difference

aggregation.notes: Hoaxy: sharing of fact-checking content 'typically lags that of misinformation by 10-20 hours', characteristic lag ~13 h by lagged cross-correlation of aggregate tweet volumes. The 10-20 h range is the authors' typical range, used here as p10/p90; it is not a formally computed percentile.

deploy.notes: Proxy: time for accurate information to reach 1,500 people (true-news average). Not a direct measure of a fact-check's reach.

ai_counterfactual.basis: Illustrative. Matching a circulating claim to an existing verified ruling and routing it to the people sharing it is a short (well under 1 hour) expert task, far inside the ~17.4 h 50% task horizon in RATES.md (METR time horizon entry), and RATES.md's 'Cost of AI at fixed capability' (~40x/year cheaper) makes screening every rising claim affordable. Assumed ~1 h from first tweet to a routed correction vs the human ~13 h lag. Speed of a correction does not guarantee people accept or share it; humans still decide.
ai_counterfactual.label: illustrative

gap_summary: A false story fills a 1,500-person audience in ~10 h; the fact-check starts moving ~13 h later (10-20 h), after the audience is already reached, and truth itself needs ~60 h.
